The site is road-served with rail service available at a siding 1 nm to the southeast. Storage Facilities Facilities in the storage area include 10 gable-roofed storage build- ings (Buildings 1-10, Figure 3), 2 storage/support buildings (Buildings 11 and 12) and 5 small support buildings. The 10 storage buildings are lightly revetted on 3 sides, thereby providing moderate blast protection. Special ventilation devices are not visible off any of these buildings. One of the storage/support buildings (Building 12) as the onl large support-type building present at the site on photography At that time, a darkening of a portion of the roof near several ventilators indicated a smoke discharge from a heating or cooking facility within the building. This building was probably providin the housing and adminis- tration facilities for-,the site at that time. along with several small support buildings, the storage buildings by a security fence. at present is probably storage/support. n is ul- ing, appeared to be separated from The function of this building Security The storage area is secured by a single fence. In addition, Building 12 and the small support buildings previously mentioned are separately secured (Figure 3). Guard posts are located along the higher northern and eastern sections of the perimeter (Figures 2 and 3). Patrol paths follow the fenceline and connect these guard posts. A guardhouse/check- point is located at the entrance to the storage area. Housing and Administration The housing and administration area is located just outside the stor- age area entrance (Figure 3). Included among the facilities in this area are 1 large building which probably provides both administration and housing, an athletic field, animal pens and several other support build- ings.
